coreIdea: left<root<right at every node. Inorder=sorted. Operations are O(h) — O(log n) if balanced, O(n) worst-case (skewed).
mustRememberFormulas: Search/Insert/Delete: O(h), O(log n) balanced, O(n) worst-case
Distinct BSTs with n keys = Catalan number C(n)
Sorted-order insertion → fully skewed tree, height n-1
Range query reporting k elements: O(h+k)
Preorder→Postorder BST trick: partition by value (root vs <root vs >root), no inorder needed

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: sequence of numbers to insert into empty BST
candidate 'examined nodes' sequence, asked if valid search path
preorder given asked for postorder (or inorder-validity check)
worst-case complexity of BST operation asked

commonTrapsQuickList: BST complexity is O(log n) ONLY if balanced is stated/guaranteed — else assume worst-case O(n)
Preorder+Postorder-only trick for BST works BECAUSE of the ordering property — general trees need inorder too
Search-path validity needs the FULL cumulative range check, not just pairwise ordering
Distinct BST count = Catalan number, not n! or 2^n
highYieldPyqLessons: Insertion-trace (10/36) and operation-complexity (10/36) together are ~56% of this topic — practice both the mechanical build AND the balanced-vs-skewed judgment call.
'Inorder = sorted' is the single most reused BST fact across every pattern in this topic — internalize it completely.
